summary.text: SLICE is a microgravity investigation that aims to better understand the structure and stability of laminar diffusion flames, using fan-driven flow duct hardware with exchangeable burner tubes.

geometry.text: Exchangeable burner tubes in a fan-driven flow duct; burner diameter is a studied factor.

flow.text: Controlled coflow air conditions; coflow velocity is a studied factor.

measurements.text: Integrated sensors for flow rates and temperature; high resolution camera still images with overlaid sensor data.

hardware.text: SLICE apparatus: fan-driven flow duct, exchangeable burner tubes, integrated sensors.

claims.text: The investigation aims to better understand the structure and stability of laminar diffusion flames in microgravity.
The investigation aims to determine liftoff velocity limits for different fuels and burner diameters.
The investigation aims to quantify the effects of microgravity on flame length and radiative heat loss compared to normal gravity conditions.
The investigation aims to validate numerical models for flame dynamics, soot production, and thermal radiation in non-premixed flames.
The investigation hypothesizes that flame structure and stability in microgravity are significantly influenced by burner diameter, coflow velocity, and fuel composition.
The source states that insights into flame stability and behavior are intended to enhance fire safety.

limitations.text: This draft cites PSI metadata and no PDF text. The packet also includes official table passages whose findings have not been incorporated or reviewed.

modeling_resources.description: An experimental table file may document test parameters; the metadata names fuels, burner diameter and coflow velocity as factors of interest. No model is claimed to exist or be validated.
